II22A-01.note: Calder (salt, quiet) below Ellery (noisy, no salt) is the only noise-against comparison. D (Brenlow < Calder) and A support noise; B is confounded. A and C mirror each other along the noise axis, which a test-wise student could notice.

II22A-02.note: Cassel vs Fairlie isolates fungi in full sun. D (Ardel > Cassel) is tempting because it names the adults' plots, but it varies shade, not fungi; B and C vary shade.

II22A-03.note: Bypass (traffic, no lamps) earlier than lit quiet lanes cuts against lamps. A and C support lamps; B is confounded (downtown has both). A student who skims may take A or C as weakening by reading the comparison backwards.

II22A-04.note: Each distractor fails exactly one condition; C (R-8) passes the temperature test and is the most tempting, failing only on salt (70). D's 90 in salt is struck on sight.

II22A-05.note: C (44 of 90) is the near-miss just under half; B is obviously low. One row with a half-check decides it.

II22A-06.note: Bramley (2,200 m, 6.0) below Carrick (1,800 m, 6.4). D is tempting because it leads with Bramley but compares it to a lower site it exceeds. B and C are on-trend increases, struck on sight; the key is the only option where the first-named value is larger but the site is lower.

II22B-01.note: North-cliff July (rain, no freeze-thaw) over north March (freeze-thaw) weakens. A, B and D all favour the freeze-thaw window, so a test-wise student can spot the one option that favours a non-freeze-thaw period; D is the most tempting since it also mentions July.

II22B-02.note: Sealed wool (lining gas only) over ventilated cotton (city air only) supports wool. D is tempting because both are wool cases, but ventilated-faster supports city air; C reverses the key's design.

II22B-03.note: Iselund pre-plant normal years erupting less than post-plant normal years weakens the pumping claim. C has the same shape on the unpumped field and is beside the point; B mixes a drought window with a pre-plant window; A supports Lark.

II22B-04.note: Garvik is deepest (64 m) and lost 19 days vs Hesk's 27. All four options show Hesk losing more than the comparison lake, so distractors are accurate but beside the point; student must find the deepest lake.

II22B-05.note: Ivarsby is the only young-sediment well over 100 m. B (Haldor, 130 m, 27) is most tempting: deep and over the limit, but old sediment. Options omit depth and sediment, forcing a lookup.

II22B-06.note: Joskar (51 km, 22 cm) thicker than Ilvikmoen (38 km, 14 cm). B, C and D all show the expected thinning; B is the only mildly tempting one because it involves Joskar.

II22C-01.note: Nolvaston (breakfast, tardiness unchanged) over Rossmere isolates breakfast. A is the confounded comparison and the most tempting; C and D favour Okafor.

II22C-02.note: Pruett (radio only) over Nantle (contact only) weakens face-to-face. B and C support Paredes; A is confounded. Requires building the east/west x school matrix.

II22C-03.note: Fourth floor is the only lottery floor with real daylight. D (third floor, lottery but blank wall) is the strongest distractor; C (seniority floor with daylight) is the confounded one.

II22C-04.note: Nuskirk 7/30 = 23%; others 16-18%. A (Orvel) is tempting because it has the largest absolute drop (11).

II22C-05.note: Medlow: 45 shoppers/vendor and 40% cards. Nevin (46) and Rushmere (42) clear the ratio but accept cards majority; Ossiter is under half on cards but only 35/vendor. Options omit the card %, forcing the lookup.

II22C-06.note: Quist (70 mi, 66) cheaper than Pirrock (57 mi, 72). D is tempting because it leads with Quist but compares it to a nearer, cheaper town; A and C are on-trend. Same 'nearer site named first, larger value first' phrasing as II22A-06.

II22D-01.note: Wrennick (rain-fed, no fees) vs Skarra (neither) isolates climate. B is confounded and most tempting; A favours fees; D weakens Thorvald.

II22D-02.note: Ulving (pine, damp stone) more corroded than Tamm (oak, dry timber) weakens oak. B and D support oak; C is confounded.

II22D-03.note: Same decade (1740s), both with pattern books, only river access differs. A favours pattern books; B and C cross both town and decade, and B (river 1740s vs hill 1710s) is the tempting confounded one. B and C's mismatched decades are a visible tell.

II22D-04.note: Tarrow 60/96 = 0.625; every other mill is exactly 0.70. A test-wise student may notice the three distractors share an identical ratio, making the odd one out the key without testing the 2/3 bound.

II22D-05.note: 1500s-1510s: paper steady at 19, books 6.0 to 5.1. B is the trap: paper also steady but books rose. A and C are struck once paper is checked (it fell). Table header gives no silver unit; minor.

II22D-06.note: Sollen: 1.45 s and 8.5 m3/seat. Teverin and Wrayne pass reverberation but are 7.5 m3/seat; Ulmar fails reverberation on sight. Teverin (largest volume) is most tempting.
